text:
mike: seeing a sudden spike in 5xxs for /v1/generate in eu-west-1c starting ~09:12 UTC, latency up to 6s and error rate ~18%

oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT CREATED (INC-2026-1718454321) - High error rate in eu-west-1c affecting inference serving. Paging primary oncall.

sara: confirming, logs show ELB healthcheck failures and a flurry of TCP RSTs from a subset of ENIs in azc. Metrics: targetgroup unhealthy 23% -> 47% in 3m.

leo: I'm on it. Which customers impacted? Any revenue-affecting routes?

mike: mostly hosted API traffic and a couple of Dedicated clusters pinned to eu-west-1c. Support report from ACME shows request timeouts.

jia: Route53 latencies also increasing in same region for our edge record; some DNS queries time out and clients fallback to other endpoints inconsistently.

ops-bot: Observed: EC2 instance reachability tests failing for instances with eni-attach pattern xxxxx-aa. Potential control-plane ENI reattachment churn.

leo: ok. hypothesis: network-level ENI flap in azc causing ELB targets to fail health checks and trigger Route53 partial degradations.

eng-runtime: can we switch traffic off azc? We have routing policies per-region and per-az failover in the smart router. If we flip prefer-region to eu-west-1 excluding azc, that should reduce impact.

mike: let's avoid full region shift initially. Plan: 1) raise ELB healthcheck threshold to avoid noisy failures 2) reduce Route53 TTL to 30s and bias away from azc 3) canary shift a portion of traffic to eu-west-1b/c? (but b already healthy)

jia: to be explicit: Route53 weighted record: reduce weight for azc endpoints to 10% and increase for others. I'll prepare the change.

leo: I'll coordinate oncall handover in 20m if needed. Who can change ALB target healthcheck config?

eng-runtime: I can. Proposed change: health check healthy threshold from 3->5, interval 10s->15s, unhealthy threshold 2->4 for the affected target groups. This will reduce flapping.

mike: ok make the config change, but document rollback steps. Post the CLI commands you will run.

eng-runtime: running now.

```bash
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:xxx:targetgroup/rg1 --attributes Key=slow-start.duration-seconds,Value=30 Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=120
aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:xxx:targetgroup/rg1 --health-check-interval-seconds 15 --health-check-path /health --health-check-port 8080 --healthy-threshold-count 5 --unhealthy-threshold-count 4
```

eng-runtime: changes applied to 3 target groups. Observability: ERROR rate dropping to 9% and latency median -> 320ms in 90s.

support-bot: customer ACME notified via status page: "Partial disruption in eu-west-1c affecting inference; mitigation in progress."

jia: Route53 update done: reduced weight for azc endpoints to 5% and TTL to 30s. Propagation should be quick; monitor fallback errors.

mike: seeing immediate drop in 5xx to 6%. Good. Any sign of EBS IO errors or disk stalls on the affected instances?

ops-bot: EBS metrics for that AZ show slight iops latency bump but within thresholds. No volume failure.

leo: what's the customer impact summary so far?

mike: impacted: hosted API requests routed to eu-west-1c experienced elevated errors and latency for ~12 minutes. After mitigation steps (ELB thresholds + Route53 weight shift), error rate dropped ~3x. Customers with Dedicated clusters pinned to eu-west-1c might see degraded throughput until they rotate capacity. Estimated affected requests: ~0.8% of overall traffic during window.

product-ops: recommend we open an incident status update in 15 with details and expected next steps. Also flag Dedicated customers for account outreach if they report problems.

jia: logs show a common pattern: asymmetric ARP/NAT rewriting on a subset of hosts (could be ENI firmware/regression). I'll open support case with AWS and attach our packet captures.

leo: handoff: I'm taking over incident for next shift. mike, if you can keep monitoring and liaise with AWS case, that'd be great.

mike: will do. Before handoff, checklist: 1) keep Route53 weight lowered until AWS confirms ENI stability 2) keep healthcheck thresholds raised 3) notify customers pinned to azc about potential remaining degradation 4) escalate if >5% error rate persists.

oncall-bot: HANDOFF: leo is now oncall for INC-2026-1718454321. Escalation path: leo -> sara -> eng-manager.

support-bot: posted status update: "Mitigation applied; partial routing away from eu-west-1c. AWS case opened. Monitoring ongoing."

ops-bot: AWS opened case #AWS-9876543210, ticket assigned to networking team. Preliminary root cause suspected ENI host-side firmware bug causing sporadic TX resets.

leo: after handoff I'll run a targeted drain of instances in azc (one batch) to see if that stabilizes everything, then re-evaluate whether to reintroduce weight slowly. Any objections?

mike: go ahead. make sure you respect Dedicated cluster affinity—notify owners before drain.

jia: capturing pcap and adding to AWS case. Also exporting CloudTrail events for ENI detach/attach around the timeframe.

leo: performing controlled drain now, batch 5 instances.

eng-runtime: after drain, ALB targets back to healthy 100% in 90s. ERROR rate dropped to baseline 0.6%. Good sign.

mike: great. closing status: degrade resolved after mitigations and instance drains. Next: follow-up runbook item to add automated AZ-level weight fallback and improve ENI flapping detection.

product-ops: will prepare customer postmortem and share timeline.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (INC-2026-1718454321) - Service returned to normal at 09:42 UTC. Please file a postmortem if >1hr incident or customer impact.

leo: filing a short blameless postmortem this afternoon. ACTIONS: increase Route53 quick-fail policy, add healthcheck hysteresis by default for target groups, open follow-up with AWS on ENI firmware.

mike: noted. Thanks all.
